metaDescription: Plan Dalyan river boats to Kaunos tombs and İztuzu Turtle Beach. Honest take on Sultaniye mud baths, Dalaman transfers and day trips.
quickAnswer: Dalyan's flat-bottomed wooden river boats link town jetties directly to the 4th-century BC Kaunos rock tombs, the ancient city ruins across the canal, and the 4.5-kilometre İztuzu Turtle Beach sandbar in 35 to 45 minutes. Located just 25–30 minutes from Dalaman Airport, Dalyan works best as a relaxed two-night stop rather than a rushed coach excursion.

body.text: Few corners of southwestern Türkiye pack as much geographic variety into ten kilometres as the Dalyan delta. A freshwater river winds out of Lake Köyceğiz through dense reed beds, slides past temple-fronted cliff tombs, and meets the Mediterranean across a protected loggerhead turtle nesting spit. This dalyan iztuzu guide explains how the river boats actually work, which stops deserve your time, and how to avoid the midday day-tripper crush.
How do river boats connect Dalyan, rock tombs and İztuzu Beach?

Licensed cooperative wooden river boats depart regularly from Dalyan's central waterfront jetty between roughly 09:00 and 18:00, cruising 35 to 45 minutes downstream through reed channels directly past the Kaunos cliffside rock tombs to the western jetty of İztuzu Beach. To visit the Kaunos ruins themselves, small rowboats shuttle passengers across the narrow canal from town in three minutes.
You have two distinct ways to use the river:

items: Shared cooperative shuttle (dolmuş boat): Cheap, frequent, and straightforward for reaching İztuzu Beach without paying for a full-day tour. You see the rock tombs clearly from the water on both legs.

Private wooden river boat hire: Worth the modest extra cost for couples or families. A private captain lets you stop at [Kaunos Archaeological Site](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?DistId=KAU&SectionId=KAU02) first—before the heat peaks—then linger at the beach or drift into quiet reed channels without waiting on twenty other passengers.

İztuzu turtle protection rules: İztuzu is one of Türkiye's most critical Caretta caretta (loggerhead) nesting beaches, monitored year-round by [DEKAMER (Sea Turtle Research, Rescue and Rehabilitation Center)](https://dekamer.org.tr/index-eng.html) at the eastern end of the sandbar. The beach closes to humans from 20:00 to 08:00 during the May–October nesting season, and umbrellas are prohibited inside staked nesting zones.

body.text: Skip the "turtle-spotting" boats that dangle blue crab meat on strings to lure turtles to the hull; visit [DEKAMER's rehabilitation centre](https://dekamer.org.tr/about.html) at the road-access end of İztuzu instead to support genuine conservation work.
Are the Sultaniye mud baths worth stopping for?

For most independent travellers, no—the Sultaniye mud baths on the southwestern shore of Lake Köyceğiz are a loud, crowded stop built around package-tour boat schedules, though the adjacent 39°C sulphurous thermal spring pool is pleasant if you arrive before 09:30 or after 16:00. Skip the mud altogether if you only have one day in Dalyan.

Sultaniye has genuine ancient roots—ruins from the Kaunos era sit near the thermal source—and the mineral-rich water feels soothing in cooler spring or autumn weather. During summer midday hours, however, dozens of tour boats unload hundreds of passengers into small concrete mud enclosures at once. If you do go, wear dark old swimwear, remove all silver jewellery (sulphur tarnishes silver immediately), and rinse thoroughly in the thermal shower before swimming in the lake.
How far is Dalyan from Dalaman Airport?

Dalyan sits just 25 to 30 kilometres northwest of [Dalaman Airport (DLM)](https://dhmi.gov.tr/Sayfalar/Havalimani/Dalaman/AnaSayfa.aspx), making it one of the shortest airport transfers on the Turquoise Coast at 25 to 35 minutes by private car or taxi. Because there is no direct airport bus into Dalyan itself, public transit requires taking a shuttle to Ortaca and switching to a local dolmuş.

That proximity makes Dalyan an intelligent first or last stop when flying through DLM—especially after a late evening landing or before an early morning departure. Compare DLM against Antalya for wider coastal routes in our [Dalaman vs Antalya Airport guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/dalaman-vs-antalya-airport).
Can you visit Dalyan as a day trip from Fethiye or Marmaris?

Yes, Dalyan is 60 kilometres (50–60 minutes by car) from Fethiye and 85 kilometres (75–90 minutes) from Marmaris, making an independent self-drive or private-driver day trip very feasible. Avoid large organised coach-and-boat tours from Marmaris, which spend more time on transit and mud-bath queues than at Kaunos or İztuzu.
If you are continuing west after Dalyan, pair it with a quieter peninsula stay using our [Bozburun and Selimiye retreat guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/bozburun-selimiye-guide).

faq.q: Can you drive directly to İztuzu Beach instead of taking a river boat?
faq.a: Yes. A scenic 12-kilometre paved road runs from Dalyan past Lake Sülüngür to the eastern end of İztuzu Beach, where DEKAMER's sea turtle rehabilitation centre and a municipal car park are located. Taking the boat one way and a dolmuş the other is also popular.

faq.q: How much time do you need at Kaunos Ancient City?
faq.a: Allow 90 minutes to two hours. After crossing the river by rowboat, walk 15 minutes uphill to the ticket gate, then explore the well-preserved Roman theatre, Byzantine basilica, baths, and harbour agora overlooking the silted-up ancient bay.

faq.q: Can you climb up to the Dalyan rock tombs?
faq.a: No. Access to the 4th-century BC Carian-Lycian cliff tombs is strictly closed to protect the carved stone facades. The clearest views are from a river boat directly below or from Dalyan's waterfront promenade at dusk when the tombs are illuminated.

faq.q: When is the best time to see sea turtles at İztuzu Beach?
faq.a: Loggerhead turtles nest at night from May to July, and hatchlings emerge from July through September—all strictly after the beach closes at 20:00. Daytime visitors have the highest chance of seeing rescued turtles up close at DEKAMER's rehabilitation tanks.

faq.q: Is Dalyan suitable for swimming in the river?
faq.a: Locals swim at Lake Köyceğiz and calm upstream pockets, but the main Dalyan canal carries heavy boat traffic and strong currents near the estuary. Save swimming for İztuzu Beach's Mediterranean side or the clear coves around Ekincik Bay.

faq.q: How many nights should you stay in Dalyan?
faq.a: Two nights is the sweet spot: one full day for Kaunos ruins, a private river boat, and İztuzu Beach, plus a relaxed second morning for Lake Köyceğiz or an unhurried drive onward to Göcek, Fethiye, or the Bozburun Peninsula.
